case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: S.R.B.R. v. Harrison County Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed a family court's termination of parental rights, holding that the petitioner must prove at least one of the grounds enumerated in Section 93-15-103(3) by clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: The guardian ad litem's weighing of durable legal custody against adoption shows how Mississippi courts choose between guardianship-style permanency and termination.
key_cases.quote: the petitioner must prove by clear and convincing evidence at least one of the grounds enumerated

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed an award of custody to third-party custodians over the natural father, holding that the presumption favoring a natural parent is overcome by a clear showing of unfitness.
key_cases.relevance: States the unfitness showing required before a third-party custody or guardianship arrangement can become the child's permanent placement.
key_cases.quote: it has been stated many times that this presumption can be overcome by a clear showing that the parent is unfit

key_cases.holding: The Court held the chancery court properly had subject-matter jurisdiction over a guardianship petition after the youth court voluntarily terminated its own jurisdiction under Section 43-21-151(2).
key_cases.relevance: Guardianship as a permanency outcome in Mississippi runs through chancery court, which can only act once youth court jurisdiction ends.
key_cases.quote: The plain language of the Act does allow the youth court to terminate its jurisdiction of a case.

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the award of custody to the natural father over the maternal grandmother and declined to change the established grounds for rebutting the natural-parent presumption.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the boundary between kinship permanency and the constitutionally protected position of the natural parent.
key_cases.quote: we find no legally compelling reason to alter or abandon our established standards for rebuttal of the natural-parent presumption

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the youth court's grant of durable legal custody of a chronically abused child to her long-time foster parents, but reversed the portion of the judgment permanently relieving the Department of Human Services of any further involvement, holding that durable legal custody leaves the parents' residual rights intact and ends only the mandatory annual dispositional reviews, not the youth court's jurisdiction or the Department's ability to monitor.
key_cases.relevance: The Supreme Court's construction of durable legal custody under Sections 43-21-609 and 43-21-613, Mississippi's guardianship-style permanency device, which the youth court itself described as similar to a chancery guardianship.
key_cases.quote: The fact that under durable legal custody the parent retains some form of residual rights and responsibilities is a vital and obvious distinction to termination of parental rights.

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of the Dissolution of the Marriage of Leverock and Hamby: Pendleton v. Leverock
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the chancellor's refusal to terminate the father's parental rights but reversed the award of custody to him, holding the record established desertion so that the natural-parent presumption was rebutted and custody had to be redetermined through an on-the-record Albright best-interests analysis.
key_cases.relevance: Third-party permanency becomes available only once the natural-parent presumption is rebutted, and even then custody turns on an on-the-record best-interests analysis rather than on the caregiver's status.
key_cases.quote: This presumption in favor of a natural parent has long been recognized, and Tony is entitled to it unless there is proof that he has relinquished it.

extended_foster_care_age: To 20 under youth court jurisdiction (Miss. Code § 43-21-151(2)); to 21 only if MDCPS petitions the chancery court before the 20th birthday (MDCPS Foster Care Policy, Section D, F. Custody Beyond Age 20)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met
